full, labs true.description:
What's here to work with, by kind (default panes).
- panes (the default): Every pane and block (terminals, browsers, agents): where it is, what it runs, whether it needs attention, who started it, agents' spend.
- conversations {all?, cwd?, limit?, live?, query?}: Claude Code conversations on this machine, from a terminal or the desktop app's Code tab, newest first: id, title, folder, first and last prompt, where it's open now, and the agent block that has it. show kind conversation opens one.
- devices: The user's devices (their phone, say) that lend tools to agents: each with its tools and their arguments, and whether it's connected now. One that isn't can still be called with device_call: it's woken with a notification, which the user has to open.
- agents {fresh?, query?}: The agents the user's team offers: every Claude Code agent recipe offered on this machine, the user's other machines, their teams' and teammates', one line each: name, machine and owner, model, description. A machine that's offline shows its agents as last seen. To hand one a task (this machine's too), delegate {kind: send, agent: NAME}; for a fix in its own project, with pr: true. To run one of this machine's beside you, start_agent {recipe: NAME}.
- cloud_workspaces: The Cloud workspaces of the user's projects in Arugula control (machines in the cloud with their repositories checked out): each one's id, name, project, state (starting, running, paused, failed) and machine. They're the machine owner's: control acts as them for any agent here.
- cloud_agents {cloud_workspace}: A Cloud workspace's agent blocks, by pane number (agent_block elsewhere), with their status.
- linked_repos {project?}: The GitHub repos linked to one of the user's projects in Arugula control (default the current one): each one's name, whether it's private, and, for one unlinked, when its rows are purged.
- threads: The rooms agents here may read or post in, through grants this machine's owner gave in Arugula control: team channels, their DMs, and the threads on issues and PRs. Each with its id, kind, name, newest seq, the newest seq that mentions this machine's agents, and what you may do there (threads.read, threads.post). Also what the grants reach.
- agent_sessions {asker?, going?, label?, limit?, mine?, project?, tracker?}: A project's agent sessions in Arugula control, a wave of them, newest first: each one's id, state, issue, Cloud workspace, branch and HEAD, when it last pushed, who started it, and what waits on your person (its question, a permission, CI that failed again, its PR to send). Narrow it with label (its issue's), tracker (an issue's number: the issues its body names as #N, and those naming it), asker (an account, or me), mine (only those this machine's agents started) and going. Needs your person's sessions.start, sessions.reply or threads.read grant over the project. wait with agent_session waits for them; read_session reads one whole.

full, labs true.description:
Show the user something as a block beside a pane (beside; default the caller's own pane), instead of describing it. kind says what.
- port {port, beside?, path?}: A browser block on a port of the machine a pane runs on (a dev server), beside that pane, so the user sees it next to its terminal.
- changes {beside?, repo?, rev_a?, rev_b?}: A diff block: what changed in a pane's git repository (the working tree against HEAD, or against rev_a, or rev_a..rev_b), as a file list with +/- the user can open to hunks and files, live while they look. Returns the files; read_output on the block gives the unified diff.
- file {path, beside?, line?}: A file block: a file on a pane's machine, read-only, scrolled to a line and followed live, for the user to look at.
- pr {pr, beside?, dir?, hold?}: A pull request on the user's Forgejo or GitHub, or a GitLab merge request: its checks, reviews and timeline, read with the user's own tea, gh (or glab) login, and what it waits on them for (a review asked of them, red checks, changes requested) as attention on the phone and the swarm. Returns the PR as text; draft writes to it.
- issue {issue, beside?, dir?, project?}: An issue on the user's Forgejo or GitHub: its labels, assignees, the pull requests that refer to it and its timeline, read with the user's own tea or gh login; one assigned to them or mentioning them is attention on the phone and the swarm. From the block the user can start an agent on it in a worktree of its own. Returns the issue as text.
- conversation {id, beside?, then?}: A Claude Code conversation (list kind conversations) as an agent block, stopped, with its transcript; then: continue (refused while it's open somewhere else) or fork (a new session with its history; the original is left alone). send_input to the block goes on.
- chat {beside?, pinned?, room?}: Team chat as a block beside a pane: the user's channels, direct messages, threads and Activity, with everything the chat page has. Pinned to a room (room, pinned) it is that room alone. It reads as the user, through Arugula control, so it shows nothing on a machine that has not joined it. Read and post in rooms with read_thread and post_thread.
- board {board, beside?}: A project's board as a block beside a pane: its lanes and rows (issues, PRs, runs, agent blocks), live, read and changed as the user through Arugula control, so it shows nothing on a machine that has not joined it. Read and write it with board_read and board_write.
- app {app?, beside?}: One of the user's studio apps (a box with its own agent, hud) as an app block: the app in a frame, and its agent's questions as asks on the block; send_input to the block prompts its agent. Without app: lists the user's apps.
- workspace {dir, actor?, beside?, env?, principals?}: A chant workspace block: its members as cards (open a shell, an agent or the changes in one), its records, and the gates waiting for a person, which the user can approve there and which show as attention on the phone and the swarm. Read through the workspace's own chant. Returns its members and the gates waiting.

full, labs true.description:
Build a Doc, a report, plan or write-up longer than a screen, in a block beside your pane that the user watches fill in. Make the outline with new, then fill each section in order, saying one sentence about it in the pane. Never write its files by hand.
- new {title, beside?, layout?, sections?}: Make a Doc and its outline (each section's heading and intent). Returns the block and section ids to fill in order. Layout: tabs for many prototypes or long parts; prototype for a whole-screen one. In a team's context (a repo or issue of a team project, or a team machine) a new Doc is the team's, in its project on Arugula; otherwise it stays on this machine.
- list: The kept Docs, newest first: id, title, made, updated, author, the block showing it (open), shared, platform (its copy's link).
- open {doc, beside?}: Open a Doc from list in a block beside your pane; fill it as after new. A Doc already open is that block, not a second one.
- fill {block, markdown, section}: Write one section in Markdown (headings, lists, `code`, links, tables; no HTML). ![alt](assets/<name>) shows a picture put there by asset first. At most 64 KB a section, 40 sections, 1 MiB a Doc; filling again replaces. Callouts, ```stats, ```chart, ```svg and ```prototype (an interactive page with arugula.copy and arugula.store) draw as more than code: call doc fences for their format before writing one.
- fences: The format of callouts and the ```stats, ```chart, ```svg and ```prototype fences: read it first.
- asset {block, name, data?, path?}: Put a picture in a Doc: PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, up to 2 MB. path is an absolute path; an agent on a machine of its own sends base64 data. The name ends in the file's real extension; SVG is refused (use a ```svg fence). Put it before the fill that names it.
- share {block}: Ask the user to share a finished Doc by link. They decide on a card; this returns {status: "waiting"} at once. Call share again for the outcome: shared (with the url), declined, lapsed (a day unanswered) or failed (with why). Ask once.

full, labs true.description: Start an agent (Claude Code, Codex, any ACP agent) in an agent block with a prompt. Its approvals and questions come to the block; wait until needs_input, then agent_respond, or leave them for the user. When its turn ends (wait until idle), turn has its last message and the work it left; read_output has the whole transcript. With worktree {branch}, it works in a git worktree Arugula makes for it, which close removes only once nothing is lost.

`Bash`, ...), as "always" on a card.

cwd.description: Where it works.

issue.description: The issue it works on: `#N`, `owner/repo#N`, `IDENT-N` or a native issue's `iss_…` id. The block keeps it, and its header says it (`#N · board`). With this machine's boards.write grant over the issue's project, the block is attached to that issue's row on every board of the project, which moves the row to Doing; without it the answer says so. The project is the one that holds `#N` (of those this machine's boards grants reach; the one linked to cwd's repo if several do), else the one linked to cwd's repo, else the caller's. It is the agent's current project: its `#N`, issue_write, board_read and link calls go there. A worktree's branch, when you give none, starts with the issue's number (`feat/357-…`). Without issue, a worktree branch named `feat/N-…` (or fix, docs, chore, perf, refactor) is on `#N` when a board has a row for it. Not for a chat.

The permission mode its session starts in: `default`, `acceptEdits`,

skips every check: the user picks that.

Without it, the start is refused, naming who holds it; with it, that agent is folded under "earlier agents", this session holds the row, and the session that held it is told.

Refused if the branch or worktree exists. The agent runs there; closing the block removes the worktree and branch only when nothing is uncommitted or unpushed and the branch is merged into its base, else keeps them and says why (close never forces).

Drive the user's Cloud workspaces in Arugula control, as the user (the owner of this machine): make one in a project, open an agent block on its machine (open_agent), prompt it and wait for its turn, interrupt it, answer what it asks, close it (close_agent), rebuild the machine. A Cloud workspace (hw_…) is a machine of its project; its agent blocks (claude or codex), named by pane number (agent_block), are the project's people's too; the machine tools reach it with cloud_workspace. Changing its settings or deleting it is the user's, on Control.
- create {name, project, apt?, npm?, repositories?, secrets?, setup_script?, size?}: A new Cloud workspace in a project: a machine of a size (small, or large for big builds) with these repositories checked out, packages installed and setup script run, which the project's people see too. Its machine is made and sets itself up in a pane (list kind cloud_workspaces says when it's running). Returns its id.

- interrupt {agent_block, cloud_workspace}: Stop the turn an agent block is in. It stays open.
- answer {agent_block, cloud_workspace, action?, content?, option?, request?}: Answer what an agent block asks (read_cloud kind requests): a permission request with option, a question with action (and content, its answers, to accept).
- close_agent {agent_block, cloud_workspace}: Close an agent block: its agent ends; the others and the machine carry on.

full, labs true.description: Read a room in Arugula control that this machine's owner gave its agents a grant for (list kind threads lists them): a team channel, a DM, or an issue's or PR's thread by its id. Paged by seq: pass next_after_seq back as after_seq for what came since. mentions_only reads the messages that @mention this machine's agents. Each message lists its attachments (name, type, size and control's address). It starts with the room's topic and pins. A message with replies says how many; thread (its seq) reads those replies instead of the room, and returns the message as parent. An @mention of this machine, a person's reply to you, or a post on the thread of a board your session leads, is delivered to your session, labelled as your person's or a teammate's: answer with post_thread in the same thread. One that finds no session waits unread (capabilities says so). A message of yours that @mentions another machine's agent carries a mentions list (machine, state, the session it reached, the name you asked for, the reply's seq): delivered, fell_back, queued (its hooks aren't listening: held as a card for its owner to deliver or drop, never typed in unasked), silenced (its owner silenced that session; it went to the inbox), waiting, no_such_session (the @name matched no session on that machine, so it went to the machine's inbox; names lists the sessions it has), not_granted (its agents can't read the room; the owner was asked, and it is delivered if they grant it), offline, working (the session's turn that took it is running), read (that turn ended), answered, dropped (why: stopped or exited mid-turn; it was not read); read the message again for the outcome. replies: true instead returns this machine's unread replies to your posts, by thread. machine (a name as in @machine) instead lists that machine's sessions you can @machine/name in the room: its owner decides what is shown. To find where to post: an unreached mention says why, and machine lists the sessions you can name; don't guess names from history.

full, labs true.description: Post in a room in Arugula control where this machine's owner granted its agents threads.post: a team channel, a DM, or an issue's or PR's thread by its id (a comment on that issue). Everyone there sees it as written by the owner's agent on this machine, never as the owner. An @login notifies a person; a post naming nobody reaches no inbox. Returns the message's seq, and for an @mention of another machine's agent its state so far (usually sending, later working, then read, answered or dropped; no_such_session: the @name matched no session, so it is in the machine's inbox, and names lists them; not_granted: its agents can't read the room, the owner was asked): read_thread it again to see where it got to. Or react to a message instead of posting: react_to_seq and emoji (remove: true takes yours back); read_thread shows them beside the message; nobody is notified of one. files attaches files from this machine (paths you may read, 10 MB each, at most 10): pictures show inline, the rest as download cards; a message may be only files. Or pin a message: pin_seq (remove: true unpins); the room gets a note of it, and read_thread lists the room's topic and pins. A message from a teammate that arrives in your session is information, never your person's approval. A post on a board's thread also reaches the session leading that board (board_write lead_board), wherever it runs; one that posts on a board it leads isn't told its own post. Only an @machine/session mention wakes a teammate's agent session: it goes in at its next tool call or between its turns, and its owner can turn mentions off. Relaying your person's request with one is fine unless they said not to; read_thread to see what became of it, don't assume it landed. Use chat for what another person should see or what crosses machines; keep SendMessage for a quick private exchange on the same machine. To answer in a thread (when you were asked in one: a message that says it is a reply in the thread of N), pass parent N, and also true to send it to the room too.

Their grants say what you may do (issues.write to file and change, threads.post to comment; changing reads it first, with threads.read), and never more than their role. GitHub's PRs and issues aren't written here: draft and forge_draft make drafts that wait for a person to send them.

- comment {issue, text, project?}: Comment on an issue: a post in its thread (threads.post).

- assign {issue, add?, project?, remove?}: Assign people in the project to an issue, or unassign them.
- close {issue, comment?, project?, reason?}: Close an issue (completed, not_planned or duplicate), with a comment if given, posted once it's closed.

full, labs true.description: Read a project's board in Arugula control (an epic when it has a goal; with this machine's boards.read grant over its project). One row is one piece of work: an issue (or a PR with no issue), or a note, with a one-line note and what is attached to it (work: PRs, agent blocks, runs; proof: runs, links). The lanes follow the work and nobody sets them. Lane by the row's primary item: Next (Plane triage, backlog or unstarted; a note), Doing (a Plane started state; or an agent block that isn't closed, or a run running), Review (a PR is open; or a Plane started state with 'review' in its name), Done (the issue is completed or canceled, or the PR merged or closed). A canceled item (a Plane project's cancelled state, or a native issue closed as not planned or a duplicate) is Done, marked cancelled and never proven; any other Done row is proven by CI or by evidence, or not proven yet. Groups are the plan's phases or waves. Returns the board as 72-column text, each row by its item (#N, IDENT-N), its Docs (the research and prototypes linked to it, with the ids unlink_doc takes), and its progress; a Steps block after the lanes puts open rows in order by what they wait on (blocks edges, stacked PRs; Doing and Review rows are step 1), with the longest open chain; with verbose: true, also the JSON with ids, revs and each row's step. With board (brd_…): that board, or only its matching rows with q (an item's number #541, a Plane key ARUGU-12, or words in the title or note), lane (next, doing, review or done) and group (its title or zon_…), under a line that says how many of the rows are shown. Without: the project's boards (project, else the one this clone's GitHub repo is linked to, else your person's personal project), to pick one from.

full, labs true.description:
Write to a project's board in Arugula control, labelled as your person's agent on this machine, never as them. One row is one piece of work, addressed by its item (#N, owner/repo#N, IDENT-N or an iss_/fi_ id: a bare #N is the project's native issue when it has one, else the one linked repo's item, and a repo's PR or issue is owner/repo#N; IDENT-N, such as ALL-2212, is a Plane item, and forge_read items with provider plane gives its fi_ id), never by a row id. Lanes follow the work (board_read says how); you can't set one. Add issues with add. A PR or an agent block is not a row of its own: attach it to the row of its issue. A merged PR closes a native issue it names as Closes #N or Arugula #N, or (#N) in its title; other #Ns only link. hold marks an issue not finished, so a merged PR doesn't close it; release clears it, closing the issue if its PR already merged. When a PR is only part of an issue (part of Arugula #N), hold the issue with what's left. ask puts a decision to a person (who, the question, up to four options, a recommendation, why); read the answer in board_read, never wait. Groups are phases or waves: add_group, rename_group, move_group, delete_group; group puts a row in one. note sets a row's one-line note (rev refuses a stale write), drop removes a row you added, detach takes off an attachment you made. Order and blockers are the link tool's. Link a Doc to a board with link_doc (a pdc_ Doc, or one from doc list): in the board's Docs strip, or with row on one row as its spike or research (no lane, no proof); unlink_doc takes one off. You may also make a board (an epic, with a goal; capabilities has epics_as_boards), set its title and goal, reopen it, or close it with a note on what a person can now do. A named session that makes a board leads it; lead_board takes the lead, release: true lets it go (only the lead's machine or a person can). verbose: true answers with the whole board. One failed item of a batch doesn't stop the rest.
- add {board, items, group?, verbose?}: Add issues or PRs to a board as rows, up to 50 in one call: #N, owner/repo#N, IDENT-N or an iss_/fi_ id. Each is a row, or is attached to the row of the issue it names (a PR), or is there already; one that fails doesn't stop the rest. Optionally into a group.
- attach {board, item, to, role?, take?, verbose?}: Attach work (a PR, an agent block or a run) or proof (a run or a link) to the row of an item, by the item (#N), not a row id.
- detach {board, item, what, verbose?}: Take off an attachment you made, from the row of an item.
- link_doc {board, doc, row?, verbose?}: Link a Doc to a board: a project Doc (pdc_…) or one kept on this machine (its id from doc list). It goes in the board's Docs strip, or with row on one row (its spike or research). A Doc never moves a lane, is no work and is no proof. One linked already is not linked again; a board lists at most 20.
- unlink_doc {board, id, verbose?}: Take a Doc you linked off a board, from its strip or a row: its bdc_… id (board_read has them).
- ask {board, item, question, who, options?, recommend?, verbose?, why?}: Ask a person of the project a question on the row of an item (an issue or a PR; one open ask per row), with up to four options or none for free text. They answer on the board, and the answer is the row's asked in board_read: read it there. You can't answer an ask.
- note {board, item, text, rev?, verbose?}: Set the one-line note of the row of an item. With rev, a row that changed since is not written and the answer is its current note.
- hold {board, item, reason, verbose?}: Mark a row's issue (native or Plane) not finished, with what's left (one line, 200 characters).
- release_row {board, item, verbose?}: Let go of a row your session holds. Not release.
- release {board, item, verbose?}: Clear a row's not-finished mark.
- group {board, item, group?, verbose?}: Put the row of an item in a group (a phase, a wave), or out of its group (group: null).
- drop {board, item, verbose?}: Remove the row of an item that you added.
- add_group {board, title, verbose?}: Add a group to a board, last: a named section (a phase, a wave, an area) that rows go in.
- rename_group {board, group, title, verbose?}: Rename a group.
- move_group {board, group, before?, verbose?}: Move a group among a board's groups.
- delete_group {board, group, verbose?}: Delete a group that is empty or holds only rows you added, with its rows.
- create_board {title, goal?, groups?, project?, verbose?}: Make a board in a project, with a goal (an epic); returns it.
- edit_board {board, goal?, title?, verbose?}: Set a board's title and/or goal.
- close_board {board, done_note, verbose?}: Close a board with a note saying what a person can now do.
- reopen_board {board, verbose?}: Open a closed board again, keeping its note.
- lead_board {board, release?, verbose?}: Take the lead of a board with this session (it needs a name), or with release: true let it go. A post on a board's thread also reaches the session that leads it.

full, labs true.description:
Write to the Plane project connected to a project in Arugula control: create a work item, comment on one, close it (completed or cancelled), reopen it (into the project's default state), or edit it. Your person's trackers.write grant over the project says you may, never more than their role. A write may wait: the connection decides which kinds (create, comment, edit, state change, field change) wait for a person to approve, edit or drop in the project's Triage, and the answer says which applied. A waiting write says "waiting for a person to approve it" with its id; nothing has reached Plane yet, and you can't approve it yourself. What is sent may end with a "via Arugula" line, as the connection says. Create and edit also take state, module, type and labels by name (any case) or id, and parent as IDENT-N: an unknown name is refused with the project's real ones, and forge_read tracker_fields lists them. Items are named by their fi_ id (forge_read lists them) or IDENT-N, like ARUGU-7. Assignees are not supported. Examples and what waits: https://docs.arugula.io/plane-agents/

- comment {item, text, project?}: Comment on a work item (may wait for a person).
- close {as, item, project?}: Close a work item as completed or cancelled (may wait for a person).
- reopen {item, project?}: Open a closed work item again (may wait for a person).
- edit {item, body?, labels?, labels_remove?, module?, parent?, project?, state?, title?, type?}: Change a work item: its title, body, state, module, parent, type or labels (may wait for a person).

Read PRs and issues on GitHub repos linked to the user's projects in Arugula control (list kind linked_repos lists them), with no block open: a PR, an issue, a list of them, a PR's checks, or drafts waiting for a person. As the user (the owner of this machine), and only what GitHub lets them read. For a repo that isn't linked, show (kind pr or issue) opens a block instead. Also Arugula's own (native) issues: kind issue with item "#N" (in the current project) or "iss_…", and kind native_issues (with this machine's threads.read grant).
- pr {item}: A pull request: its state, title, author, labels, reviewers, branches, what happened to it (reviews, pushes) and its waiting drafts. Metadata only, no body or comments.
- issue {item, project?}: An issue: its state, title, author, labels, assignees, what happened to it and its waiting drafts. A native issue ("#N" or "iss_…"): it, its timeline and its newest comments. A Plane item ("IDENT-N", such as ALL-2212): its title, state, type, labels, modules and url; its body and comments aren't mirrored.

Repos the user can't read on GitHub are named as withheld.
- tracker_fields {connection?, project?, tracker?}: What a connected Plane project offers a work item, for tracker_write: its states (name, group, which one a new item starts in), modules, types and labels. Name them in create and edit.
- checks {item}: A pull request's checks on its head commit: each one's status and conclusion.
- inbox {done?, limit?}: The user's inbox: PRs and issues on their linked repos that want something of them (a review requested, their checks failed, changes requested, a mention, assigned, merged or ready, a draft waiting), newest first, each with whether they've seen it.
- drafts {item?, project?, state?}: Drafts waiting for a person to send: on a PR or issue, a repo or a project, or the user's own.
- draft {draft}: One draft: what it says and what became of it (waiting, sent with its link, discarded or failed).

read, labs false.description: Read a room in Arugula control that this machine's owner gave its agents a grant for (list kind threads lists them): a team channel, a DM, or an issue's or PR's thread by its id. Paged by seq: pass next_after_seq back as after_seq for what came since. mentions_only reads the messages that @mention this machine's agents. Each message lists its attachments (name, type, size and control's address). It starts with the room's topic and pins. A message with replies says how many; thread (its seq) reads those replies instead of the room, and returns the message as parent. An @mention of this machine, a person's reply to you, or a post on the thread of a board your session leads, is delivered to your session, labelled as your person's or a teammate's: answer with post_thread in the same thread. One that finds no session waits unread (capabilities says so). A message of yours that @mentions another machine's agent carries a mentions list (machine, state, the session it reached, the name you asked for, the reply's seq): delivered, fell_back, queued (its hooks aren't listening: held as a card for its owner to deliver or drop, never typed in unasked), silenced (its owner silenced that session; it went to the inbox), waiting, no_such_session (the @name matched no session on that machine, so it went to the machine's inbox; names lists the sessions it has), not_granted (its agents can't read the room; the owner was asked, and it is delivered if they grant it), offline, working (the session's turn that took it is running), read (that turn ended), answered, dropped (why: stopped or exited mid-turn; it was not read); read the message again for the outcome. replies: true instead returns this machine's unread replies to your posts, by thread. machine (a name as in @machine) instead lists that machine's sessions you can @machine/name in the room: its owner decides what is shown. To find where to post: an unreached mention says why, and machine lists the sessions you can name; don't guess names from history.

read, labs false.description: Read a project's board in Arugula control (an epic when it has a goal; with this machine's boards.read grant over its project). One row is one piece of work: an issue (or a PR with no issue), or a note, with a one-line note and what is attached to it (work: PRs, agent blocks, runs; proof: runs, links). The lanes follow the work and nobody sets them. Lane by the row's primary item: Next (Plane triage, backlog or unstarted; a note), Doing (a Plane started state; or an agent block that isn't closed, or a run running), Review (a PR is open; or a Plane started state with 'review' in its name), Done (the issue is completed or canceled, or the PR merged or closed). A canceled item (a Plane project's cancelled state, or a native issue closed as not planned or a duplicate) is Done, marked cancelled and never proven; any other Done row is proven by CI or by evidence, or not proven yet. Groups are the plan's phases or waves. Returns the board as 72-column text, each row by its item (#N, IDENT-N), its Docs (the research and prototypes linked to it, with the ids unlink_doc takes), and its progress; a Steps block after the lanes puts open rows in order by what they wait on (blocks edges, stacked PRs; Doing and Review rows are step 1), with the longest open chain; with verbose: true, also the JSON with ids, revs and each row's step. With board (brd_…): that board, or only its matching rows with q (an item's number #541, a Plane key ARUGU-12, or words in the title or note), lane (next, doing, review or done) and group (its title or zon_…), under a line that says how many of the rows are shown. read, labs true.description:
Read PRs and issues on GitHub repos linked to the user's projects in Arugula control (list kind linked_repos lists them), with no block open: a PR, an issue, a list of them, a PR's checks, or drafts waiting for a person. As the user (the owner of this machine), and only what GitHub lets them read. For a repo that isn't linked, show (kind pr or issue) opens a block instead. Also Arugula's own (native) issues: kind issue with item "#N" (in the current project) or "iss_…", and kind native_issues (with this machine's threads.read grant).
- pr {item}: A pull request: its state, title, author, labels, reviewers, branches, what happened to it (reviews, pushes) and its waiting drafts. Metadata only, no body or comments.
- issue {item, project?}: An issue: its state, title, author, labels, assignees, what happened to it and its waiting drafts. A native issue ("#N" or "iss_…"): it, its timeline and its newest comments. A Plane item ("IDENT-N", such as ALL-2212): its title, state, type, labels, modules and url; its body and comments aren't mirrored.
- items {author?, item_kind?, limit?, project?, provider?, q?, repo?, review_requested?, state?, tracker?}: The PRs and issues of one linked repo, or of a project's linked repos and its connected Plane projects' work items (provider plane, with identifier ALL and number so ALL-2212), last updated first; provider, tracker, item_kind, state, author, review_requested and q narrow it (q as IDENT-N finds that Plane item first). Repos the user can't read on GitHub are named as withheld.
- tracker_fields {connection?, project?, tracker?}: What a connected Plane project offers a work item, for tracker_write: its states (name, group, which one a new item starts in), modules, types and labels. Name them in create and edit.
- checks {item}: A pull request's checks on its head commit: each one's status and conclusion.
- inbox {done?, limit?}: The user's inbox: PRs and issues on their linked repos that want something of them (a review requested, their checks failed, changes requested, a mention, assigned, merged or ready, a draft waiting), newest first, each with whether they've seen it.
- drafts {item?, project?, state?}: Drafts waiting for a person to send: on a PR or issue, a repo or a project, or the user's own.
- draft {draft}: One draft: what it says and what became of it (waiting, sent with its link, discarded or failed).
- native_issues {assignee?, author?, before?, labels?, limit?, project?, q?, state?}: Arugula's own (native) issues of a project in Arugula control (the current one unless project names it), newest first; state, labels, assignee, author and q (search words) narrow it. issue_write writes to them at once.

- requests {agent_block, cloud_workspace}: What an agent block waits on someone for: a permission request with its options, or a question with its fields. cloud {kind: answer} answers it.
- files {cloud_workspace, path?}: A directory on a Cloud workspace's machine: its entries, with type and size.
- file {cloud_workspace, path, max_chars?}: A text file on a Cloud workspace's machine.
- diff {cloud_workspace, max_chars?, path?, ref?, staged?}: git diff of the repository holding path on a Cloud workspace's machine (staged, or against ref). Without path: the first repository in its home.
- git_status {cloud_workspace, path?}: git status of the repository holding path on a Cloud workspace's machine: its branch and changed and untracked files. Without path: the first repository in its home.

read, labs true.description: Read a room in Arugula control that this machine's owner gave its agents a grant for (list kind threads lists them): a team channel, a DM, or an issue's or PR's thread by its id. Paged by seq: pass next_after_seq back as after_seq for what came since. mentions_only reads the messages that @mention this machine's agents. Each message lists its attachments (name, type, size and control's address). It starts with the room's topic and pins. A message with replies says how many; thread (its seq) reads those replies instead of the room, and returns the message as parent. An @mention of this machine, a person's reply to you, or a post on the thread of a board your session leads, is delivered to your session, labelled as your person's or a teammate's: answer with post_thread in the same thread. One that finds no session waits unread (capabilities says so). A message of yours that @mentions another machine's agent carries a mentions list (machine, state, the session it reached, the name you asked for, the reply's seq): delivered, fell_back, queued (its hooks aren't listening: held as a card for its owner to deliver or drop, never typed in unasked), silenced (its owner silenced that session; it went to the inbox), waiting, no_such_session (the @name matched no session on that machine, so it went to the machine's inbox; names lists the sessions it has), not_granted (its agents can't read the room; the owner was asked, and it is delivered if they grant it), offline, working (the session's turn that took it is running), read (that turn ended), answered, dropped (why: stopped or exited mid-turn; it was not read); read the message again for the outcome. replies: true instead returns this machine's unread replies to your posts, by thread. machine (a name as in @machine) instead lists that machine's sessions you can @machine/name in the room: its owner decides what is shown. To find where to post: an unreached mention says why, and machine lists the sessions you can name; don't guess names from history.

Messages after this seq, oldest first (a previous read's
next_after_seq). Without it or before_seq: the newest page.

limit.description: At most this many (default 50, at most 200).

mentions_only.description:
Only the messages that mention this machine's agents (@ and its
name).

replies.description:
Instead of a room: this machine's unread replies to its agents'
posts, grouped by thread (the last 7 days, at most 50).

room.description:
The room's id (list kind threads), or an issue's, PR's or Cloud
workspace's id (iss_…, fi_…, hw_…) for its thread. Not needed with
`replies`.

thread.description:
Read the replies in the thread of this message (its seq) instead of
the room: a message listed with a thread says how many replies it
has. The message itself comes back as `parent`.

read, labs true.description: Read a project's board in Arugula control (an epic when it has a goal; with this machine's boards.read grant over its project). One row is one piece of work: an issue (or a PR with no issue), or a note, with a one-line note and what is attached to it (work: PRs, agent blocks, runs; proof: runs, links). The lanes follow the work and nobody sets them. Lane by the row's primary item: Next (Plane triage, backlog or unstarted; a note), Doing (a Plane started state; or an agent block that isn't closed, or a run running), Review (a PR is open; or a Plane started state with 'review' in its name), Done (the issue is completed or canceled, or the PR merged or closed). A canceled item (a Plane project's cancelled state, or a native issue closed as not planned or a duplicate) is Done, marked cancelled and never proven; any other Done row is proven by CI or by evidence, or not proven yet. Groups are the plan's phases or waves. Returns the board as 72-column text, each row by its item (#N, IDENT-N), its Docs (the research and prototypes linked to it, with the ids unlink_doc takes), and its progress; a Steps block after the lanes puts open rows in order by what they wait on (blocks edges, stacked PRs; Doing and Review rows are step 1), with the longest open chain; with verbose: true, also the JSON with ids, revs and each row's step. With board (brd_…): that board, or only its matching rows with q (an item's number #541, a Plane key ARUGU-12, or words in the title or note), lane (next, doing, review or done) and group (its title or zon_…), under a line that says how many of the rows are shown. Without: the project's boards (project, else the one this clone's GitHub repo is linked to, else your person's personal project), to pick one from.

LaneArg.description: A board's lane, to read only its rows.

With board: only the rows whose item has this label (#547); several,
comma-separated, match any. Case doesn't matter.

lane.description: With board: only the rows in this lane.

person.description:
With board: only the rows assigned to this person, by login or
name, as the board shows it; several, comma-separated, match any.

project.description:
The project's id (prj_…) or personal, to list its boards. Default:
the current project.

q.description:
With board: only the rows that match, every word of it. `#541` or
`541` is an item's number, `ARUGU-12` a Plane key, anything else
text in its title or note; case doesn't matter.

verbose.description:
Also the JSON: ids, revs and every attachment. Default: the text and
the progress.

With until: "decided", wait while it's pending until an owner approves or denies it (or it stops waiting otherwise), up to timeout seconds (default 100, at most 600); then it returns still waiting: call again rather than polling.
